# Universal Entanglement Readout

This repository studies the exact outcome requirements of one fixed collective
entanglement detector and the finite-statistics cost of binary universality.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, result table, reading route, reproduction command.
- manuscript/main.md: connected manuscript account and proof mechanisms.
- science/model.md: authoritative model, distance convention, quantifiers, R1/R2/R3/S1.
- science/outcome_minima.md: physical quadrant, one- and two-coordinate obstructions,
  sharp qubit–qutrit criterion, marginal-rank promise, embedding corollary.
- science/collective_measurements.md: explicit six-copy permutation/reduction
  operators, certified norms, four-outcome and three-outcome POVMs.
- science/binary_rigidity.md: determinant divisibility, four-copy minimum,
  effect spectrum, and permutation-average uniqueness.
- science/sampling_cost.md: uniform fixed-k repetition lower bound, matching
  construction, and separate unrestricted total-copy benchmark.
- science/promise_gap.md: supporting logarithmic binary block-size theorem,
  majority reduction, rational filter, and uncontrolled probability margin.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: established ingredients, nearby models, and
  bounded scope of the literature comparison.
- references/references.bib: primary source metadata.
- verification/README.md: exact checks and their limits.
- verification/run_all.py: deterministic standard-library verification runner.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- m outcomes retain m-1 coordinates; one setting is not automatically one scalar.
- R1 lower bounds allow arbitrary finite k and arbitrary exact postprocessing.
- The three-outcome qubit–qutrit result requires an invertible qutrit marginal.
- Four outcomes are sufficient on all 2x3 states; larger dimensions inherit only
  the lower bound. Six-copy necessity is not proved.
- R3 minimizes over effects exactly universal on all two-qubit mixed states.
  The effect can depend on delta,eta but must retain global universality.
- R3 is Theta_k(delta^-8 log(1/eta)) at fixed k, with explicit confidence range.
  It is not a general lower bound on entanglement detection.
- S1 counts copies per block with exact probability resolution. It does not
  bound total copies, gate complexity, or the probability margin.
- The two-qubit determinant construction and key background theorems are prior
  work. Read the attribution before making an originality claim.
- Finite checks verify finite ingredients. Use the written proofs for universal
  and asymptotic statements, and do not infer mastery or peer review from them.
